readout.purpose: Live measured values in the telemetry rail (Link latency); 28px on desktop screens under 840px tall. Always core white with glow.

wordmark.purpose: The ATLAS wordmark in the top bar only, uppercase, core white with glow.

core-state.purpose: The state word on the core's disc, uppercase, scaled to the core's own width; 14px beside the phone instrument.

title.purpose: Session log title and popover title, HUD voice (uppercase).

label.purpose: Panel heads and buttons, HUD voice (uppercase). Set width with font-stretch: 125%.

body.purpose: Message bodies and the composer input, normal width, sentence case.

meta.purpose: Key-value labels, chip values, notes, counts and the bottom strip.

mono.purpose: Code blocks (13px) and API routes / file paths (11-12px), always with real casing.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: The --glow text-shadow: wordmark, clock, readout values, online node names, Atlas speaker label, plate, phone core state.

shadows.name: lit-dot
shadows.purpose: Status dots, meter fill, streaming caret, newest latency bar; amber and red versions on warn and bad chips.

shadows.name: warn-readout
shadows.purpose: Text-shadow on the Link readout when a health check fails.

shadows.name: composer-focus
shadows.purpose: Composer while focused, with a signal border.

shadows.name: log-receiving
shadows.purpose: On a 1px signal frame at 55% opacity, flashed on the session log when a reply pulse lands.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Systems sheet at 1180px and narrower (opaque ground fill).

shadows.name: core-disc
shadows.purpose: SVG filter on the core's disc layer; scan arc 8px, context arc 6px, data arc 5px, brand mark 6px.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Responses: press, hover, popover, sheet, message entrance, meters, context arc, value flash, boot overlay fade.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Travel: beam pulses and the core's glide home after boot.

motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: Reveals: panel draw-in after boot and the core's rings opening.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every button and module node on :active; suggested prompts use 0.985.

motion.name: popover-enter
motion.value: 160ms ease-out, opacity 0 + scale(0.96) to 1, origin at the node
motion.purpose: Module popover grows from its node.

motion.name: sheet
motion.purpose: Systems sheet open/close at 1180px and narrower.

motion.name: message-enter
motion.purpose: Each new message and boot log line.

motion.name: value-flash
motion.purpose: A telemetry value that just changed.

motion.name: meter-fill
motion.purpose: Context meter in the Session panel; the core's context arc uses 700ms on stroke-dasharray.

motion.name: beam-pulse
motion.value: 620ms ease-in-out, 70ms between beams; inbound pulses at most every 700ms
motion.purpose: Light travelling between the core and the session log; the log frame flashes 120ms on, 600ms off when it lands.

motion.name: panel-reveal
motion.value: 620ms ease-expo, clip-path inset from the right, 70ms stagger
motion.purpose: Panels draw in left to right after boot; 300ms fade under reduced motion.

motion.name: boot-ring-open
motion.value: 1000ms ease-expo, clip-path circle(0%) to circle(75%), 90ms stagger per layer
motion.purpose: Core layers open from the centre during boot.

motion.name: boot-glide
motion.purpose: Core returns from screen centre to its place; overlay fades 700ms.

motion.name: boot-pacing
motion.purpose: Boot log readable pacing; skipped by click, key or reduced motion.

motion.name: ring-periods
motion.value: ticks 140s cw, segments 90s ccw, data 46s cw (coupled); scan 1.1s cw (fixed)
motion.purpose: Base rotation per ring at speed 1.

motion.name: ring-speeds
motion.value: booting 2.5, standby 1, listening 1.6, thinking 3, streaming 2 + min(chunks/s / 8, 6), error 0.4, offline 0 (instant)
motion.purpose: Playback-rate multiplier per core state; eased 6% per frame toward target.

motion.name: chunk-energy
motion.value: +0.14 per chunk (cap 1), decay x0.9 per frame
motion.purpose: Disc scale 1 + 0.05*energy, opacity 0.82 + 0.18*energy; bloom scale 0.92 + 0.3*energy, opacity 0.18 + 0.7*energy.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: Streaming caret; steady under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Rings paused, no beam pulses, no boot ring-open/glide/pacing, reveal becomes a 300ms fade, message entrances and caret blink off, instant log scroll; colour, opacity and brightness pulses remain.

breakpoints.name: systems-drawer
breakpoints.purpose: Two columns; telemetry rail becomes the Systems sheet; operator, version and Modules chip hide.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: One column; core becomes a 96px status instrument; chips, strip, beams and nodes hide; log runs edge to edge.

breakpoints.name: short-desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Tighter panel padding; two notes hide.

breakpoints.name: short-desktop-tight
breakpoints.purpose: Chunk caption hides; readouts drop to 28px.

breakpoints.name: core-container
breakpoints.purpose: Node labels drop their phase line.

narrative.overview:
Atlas is a heads-up display projected onto a blue-black table: a faint 32px grid, light falling off from just left of centre, and every structure drawn in translucent cyan light rather than grey. At its centre sits the core, a stack of concentric rings that is the model made visible. It sweeps a scan arc while the model thinks, surges with every streamed chunk, spins faster with the measured stream rate, and stops dead when the backend is gone. Ten module nodes sit on its outer ring and light up only when their backend routes really exist. The spectacle is real telemetry in costume.

Density is instrument-panel high at the edges (telemetry rail, status chips, a strip of traffic numbers) and calm where reading happens. The session log on the right is a darker, quieter frame with normal-width 15px type, so a reply stays comfortable to read beside the turning core. The owner's binding reference is the cinematic holographic HUD: cyan on black, a circular core, dense panels and a boot sequence. Atlas builds its own HUD from that grammar and copies no film props or studio marks.

The world rejects the category default for chat, a conversation sidebar beside a centred transcript. Chat is the job, and it lives in the right-hand log next to the instrument that shows the model working.
keyCharacteristics: One hue family (cyan, roughly 209–239° in OKLCH) on a near-black ground; amber and red are status voices only.
Structure in light: 1px translucent cyan frames, with brighter 2px corner brackets on instrument regions.
One variable typeface, Saira, in two widths: expanded tracked capitals for labels, normal width for reading.
Glow is emission. It belongs to the core, the identity marks, the clock, live values and lit status.
The core's ring speed is coupled to app state and to the measured stream rate.
Every number is measured, labelled as an estimate, or an em dash that names the route it is waiting for.

rules.name: The Structure-in-Light Rule
rules.body: Frames, dividers, meter tracks and scrollbars are cyan at reduced alpha (line at 20%, line-strong at 42%). There are no grey borders anywhere in the world.

rules.name: The Status Voice Rule
rules.body: Cyan means live and answering. Amber means it exists but isn't working (stub, waiting, warning, fault, offline core). Red is only a dead Link chip. Amber and red are never decorative.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every ink token clears 4.5:1 on the ground and on panel glass. Ink 3, the faintest, measures about 7.3:1 on the ground and 5.4:1 on the raised tint. New text colours meet the same floor.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Expanded tracked capitals are for labels only: panel heads, chip labels, buttons, speaker names, node names, the core state, the wordmark and the plate. Anything a person reads as a sentence is normal width and sentence case.

rules.name: The Real Spelling Rule
rules.body: API routes and file paths keep their real, case-sensitive spelling in mono, even inside an uppercase HUD label (panel subheads, boot log lines, popover paths).

rules.name: The Log Keeps Its Height Rule
rules.body: When width runs out, telemetry moves into the Systems sheet before the session log gives up any height. The log and composer are never pushed below the fold.

rules.name: The Emission-Not-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Cyan glow marks light that is live: the core, the identity marks, the clock, measured values and online modules. Body text, panel heads and static frames never glow.

rules.name: The Floating-Goes-Opaque Rule
rules.body: Only the popover and the Systems sheet carry a dark drop shadow, and both switch to an opaque fill (panel solid or ground) so their text never sits over the turning rings.

rules.name: The Bracket Placement Rule
rules.body: Corner brackets mark instrument regions: a diagonal pair on telemetry panels, one top-left bracket on the session log, arcs on the core. Chips, buttons, messages and the popover carry plain 1px frames.

rules.name: The Honest Readout Rule
rules.body: A value is measured; or labelled as an estimate ("≈", "estimated", "(browser)"); or an em dash with a note naming the route and phase that will supply it. There are no placeholder numbers and no simulated graphs.

rules.name: The Coupled Rotation Rule
rules.body: The core's speed is the app's state plus the measured stream rate, never a decorative speed-up. A dead link stops the rings dead.

rules.name: The Lit-Only-When-Built Rule
rules.body: A node turns cyan only when its route answers. There is no "coming soon" glow.

rules.name: The Still-But-Readable Rule
rules.body: With reduced motion nothing rotates or travels across the screen, but every state still reads through colour and brightness.

dos: **Do** draw every frame and divider in cyan light: line (rgba(90, 205, 255, 0.2)) by default, line-strong (rgba(110, 220, 255, 0.42)) for controls and floating layers.
**Do** set labels in Saira at 125% width, uppercase, 0.14em tracking, and set everything people read at normal width in sentence case.
**Do** keep API routes and file paths in mono with their real casing.
**Do** show a missing value as an em dash with a note naming the route and phase that will supply it, and label estimates as estimates.
**Do** drive any new core behaviour from measured data through the state speed table, never from a decorative timer.
**Do** use amber for anything that exists but isn't working yet, and keep red for a dead link.
**Do** give floating layers an opaque fill and the dark drop shadow, and keep in-flow panels translucent and shadowless.
**Do** keep hover styles inside `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and give every pressable element a press scale (0.97 for buttons and nodes).
donts: **Don't** add grey borders, grey text or an untinted neutral; every neutral in the world leans toward the cyan hue.
**Don't** invent numbers, sparklines or simulated telemetry to fill a panel.
**Don't** light a module node cyan before its route answers.
**Don't** add glow to body text, panel heads or static frames.
**Don't** introduce rounded cards, pill buttons or large radii; the world is square, with a 2px concession on controls.
**Don't** let the spectacle cover the log: the session log and composer never lose height to telemetry, and rings, beams and pulses stop at the log's frame.
**Don't** add a second display or body typeface; Saira's width axis carries the hierarchy, and mono is for code and routes only.
**Don't** rebuild the chat as a conversation sidebar beside a centred transcript.
